findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit statement (and, if needed, a code change + test) confirming that transition_close.py:513 handles a None return from derive_caused_by gracefully — either it already guards for None, or B4's scope must include patching that call site.
evidence: Plan cites the call chain: 'metrics/blame.py:69 <- derive_caused_by <- transition_close.py:513'
AC4 specifies the desired outcome ('no link event is written') but does not state what transition_close.py does with None — whether it guards, logs, or propagates.
The plan does not mention any change to transition_close.py, nor does it assert that transition_close.py already guards for a None result.
findings.finding: B4 changes derive_caused_by to return None on any per-path blame failure, but the plan does not acknowledge how its sole named caller — transition_close.py:513 — handles a None return. If transition_close.py previously assumed a non-None culprit (e.g., by unconditionally writing a caused_by link or by indexing into the result), the behavior change silently breaks the bug-close path rather than hardening it.
findings.location: Scope (children) B4; AC4; plan citation 'metrics/blame.py:69 <- derive_caused_by <- transition_close.py:513'
scenarios: transition_close.py:513 calls derive_caused_by and previously always received a dict/string; after B4 it receives None on blame failure and raises AttributeError or writes a null caused_by field, breaking bug-close transitions silently.
The unit test for AC4 only covers derive_caused_by in isolation; the integration path through transition_close.py is untested, so a regression goes undetected until production.
findings.suggested_fix: In the B4 description, add: 'transition_close.py:513 already returns early / skips writing the caused_by link when derive_caused_by returns None (confirmed by <line reference>)' — or add a guard to transition_close.py as part of B4 and cover it in AC4's test.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `grep -rn 'git clone' src/` greps the unanchored word 'git' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_git'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"git":')
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the two target functions explicitly in the B5 scope line: replace 'the two authorship resolvers' with 'resolve_event_commit and resolve_position_commit (authorship.py:131, 177)' — distinguishing them from build_introducing_commit_map and build_position_commit_map, which already carry both flags.
evidence: Plan B5: 'add --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false to the two authorship resolvers' — no function names given
authorship.py:316-327: build_introducing_commit_map already has '-c log.showSignature=false' and '--no-renames' in its subprocess.run call
authorship.py:382-398: build_position_commit_map already has '-c log.showSignature=false' and '--no-renames' in its subprocess.run call
authorship.py:153-168: resolve_event_commit subprocess.run has no -c log.showSignature=false and no --no-renames
authorship.py:194-208: resolve_position_commit subprocess.run has no -c log.showSignature=false and no --no-renames
AC for B5 names 'resolve_event_commit and resolve_position_commit' as the test targets — confirming these are the intended fix sites, but the plan body does not
findings.finding: The plan's B5 body says 'add --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false to the two authorship resolvers' without naming which two functions are the targets. The codebase shows that build_introducing_commit_map and build_position_commit_map (authorship.py:316-327 and 382-398) ALREADY carry both flags in the current implementation. The two functions that are still unprotected are resolve_event_commit and resolve_position_commit (authorship.py:131-174, 177-215), which use bare --format=%H git log calls. An implementer who checks the bulk-map builders first may conclude the flags are already present and mark B5 done without touching the per-event resolvers — leaving signed-commit corruption in the exact functions the B5 AC tests.
findings.location: Scope section — child B5; authorship.py:131-174 (resolve_event_commit), authorship.py:177-215 (resolve_position_commit)
scenarios: Implementer audits authorship.py, finds --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false already present in build_introducing_commit_map and build_position_commit_map, declares B5 done, and ships without touching resolve_event_commit / resolve_position_commit — leaving signed-commit corruption unfixed in the per-event fallback path.

On a runner where a user's global gitconfig sets log.showSignature=true, resolve_event_commit returns the wrong SHA (a gpg: line instead of a 40-hex commit) for signed commits, silently producing a None authorship verdict.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the B5 scope entry to: 'B5: add `--no-renames` and `-c log.showSignature=false` to `resolve_event_commit` (authorship.py:153) and `resolve_position_commit` (authorship.py:194) — the per-event fallback resolvers, which unlike the bulk-map builders currently lack both flags.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct AC #2 to remove or replace the claim that it 'proves B3 landed before B1': either add a separate negative-case test (reconverge on a blobless runner WITHOUT merge.ours.driver defined fails or produces a warning), or restate AC #2 as 'proves B3 and B1 are both present and functional together' and add a gating mechanism (e.g. CI branch-protection rule or a pre-merge check) to enforce the ordering constraint independently.
evidence: AC #2: 'A reconverge against a diverged remote succeeds on a blobless runner (proves B3 landed before B1 and the merge driver is defined).'
Compatibility: 'with `merge.ours.driver` undefined on the runner, `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` silently degrades to a 3-way text merge of an 18 MB JSON file'
A passing AC #2 is fully compatible with B1 and B3 landing in the same merge or in reverse order, so the parenthetical claim of 'proves B3 landed before B1' is false.
findings.finding: AC #2 claims the reconverge test 'proves B3 landed before B1 and the merge driver is defined,' but a post-deployment integration test of the end state cannot distinguish simultaneous landing from correctly sequenced landing. The ordering constraint (B3 strictly before B1) is described as critical in Compatibility/Rollback (silent 3-way merge of 18 MB JSON if violated), yet no AC tests the failure mode or enforces the sequencing gate.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC #2; Compatibility and rollback section ('B3 must land **before** B1')
scenarios: A developer merges B1 and B3 simultaneously (or B1 first) — AC #2 still passes because the end-state has both, but the ordering safeguard was never enforced or detected.
The AC's parenthetical rationale misleads reviewers into thinking ordering is verified when it is not.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the Scope B4 description with AC #4: replace 'abort' with 'return None' (or 'fail closed by returning None') to make the required function contract unambiguous.
evidence: Scope B4: 'make `derive_caused_by` abort on any per-path blame failure'
AC #4: 'derive_caused_by returns None when blame fails on **any** path, rather than tallying a partial path set'
AC #4 verify step: 'asserting no link event is written' — consistent with returning None, not necessarily with raising an exception
findings.finding: Scope B4 describes the second deliverable as 'make `derive_caused_by` abort on any per-path blame failure,' but AC #4 specifies the observable behavior as 'returns None' and 'asserting no link event is written.' 'Abort' could mean raise an exception (propagating upward) or return None (fail-closed inline); an implementer reading the Scope description alone might choose exception-raising, while the AC implies silent None return.
findings.location: Scope child B4 description; Acceptance Criteria AC #4
scenarios: Implementer raises an exception in derive_caused_by on blame failure; AC #4 passes if the caller catches it and writes no event, but the interface contract differs from 'returns None'.
A unit test asserting the return value is None would fail if the function raises instead.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope B4, change 'make `derive_caused_by` abort on any per-path blame failure' to 'make `derive_caused_by` return None (writing no link event) on any per-path blame failure.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document in both B1 and B6 that B6 must land before B1 (or simultaneously) to prevent 33 MB promisor blob fetches from the .bak-retarget directory during the first blobless tickets worktree checkout, and add an ordering guard (B1 declares 'Depends on B6').
evidence: B6 states 'No dependencies' and the parent plan only says 'B6 must land before epic 0303-692c's reclaim' — no intra-epic ordering with B1 is stated.

B1-AC4 asserts 'Whole-store verify-identity on a blobless runner triggers no promisor fetch (pack count and size unchanged across the run)' — this assertion can silently fail if .bak-retarget blobs are still in the tickets tree when the blobless worktree is first checked out.

Parent plan background: '.bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json 33,025,572 bytes … materialized by every worktree checkout' — in a blobless clone this materialization triggers a promisor fetch for that blob.

B1 background: 'the later manual fetch then inherits remote.origin.partialclonefilter — that inheritance is load-bearing' — blob fetches triggered by worktree add are not covered by this claim but still incur cost.
findings.finding: B6 must land before B1 within this epic, but this intra-epic ordering constraint is undocumented in either child. When B1's blobless filter is active and B6 has not yet removed .bridge_state.bak-retarget, a `git worktree add` (or `git checkout`) of the tickets branch will trigger on-demand promisor fetches for the 33 MB .bak-retarget blobs, partially defeating B1's size savings and contradicting B1-AC4's assertion that no promisor fetch occurs during the tickets mount.
scenarios: B1 lands before B6: first blobless CI run fetches 33 MB of .bak-retarget blobs during `git worktree add tickets`, making B1-AC4's no-promisor-fetch measurement fail or mislead.
B1-AC4 is measured after B6 lands in local testing but B6 is reverted or not yet merged to the main branch — same failure mode in production CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Depends on B6' to B1's dependency list alongside 'Depends on B3', and add a note to B6 that it is a prerequisite for B1 as well as epic 0303-692c's reclaim. Optionally add a B1 pre-flight check: assert `git ls-tree HEAD:.bridge_state.bak-retarget` returns empty before declaring the blobless measurement valid.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a targeted probe/AC that runs `git blame` on at least one historical file in a blobless clone fixture (with network access matching the CI environment) to confirm lazy blob fetch succeeds — or, if it cannot, that the resulting universal None return from `derive_caused_by` is an acceptable and monitored outcome.
evidence: 'The accepted cost is stated rather than waved away: git blame over historical trees runs on the bug-close path (metrics/blame.py:69 <- derive_caused_by <- transition_close.py:513).'
No AC requires running blame against a blobless clone fixture to confirm lazy fetch succeeds or that the failure mode is graceful rather than total.
AC item 4 only tests that derive_caused_by returns None on per-path failure — it does not distinguish 'one path failed' from 'all paths failed due to missing blobs'.
findings.finding: The plan asserts that `git blame` over historical trees will 'degrade gracefully' in a blobless clone via lazy on-demand blob fetches, but no AC or spike validates that the CI runner can actually perform those on-demand fetches. If the runner's network access to the partial clone server is restricted, or the partialclonefilter is not inherited by the blame subprocess, every call to `derive_caused_by` on the bug-close path will fail — and B4's per-path abort would then suppress ALL `caused_by` links, not just incorrect ones.
findings.location: Approach section ('The accepted cost is stated rather than waved away: git blame over historical trees runs on the bug-close path') and B4 scope item
scenarios: CI runner cannot reach GitHub's partial clone server to fetch missing blame blobs — derive_caused_by returns None for every bug close, silently dropping all caused_by links.
The worktree used for blame is a detached HEAD without the partialclonefilter config propagated — blame fails 100% and B4's abort fires universally.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC to B2 (or a shared integration test) that verifies `rebar init` still sets `merge.ours.driver=true` in the worktree git config after B2's changes, exercised by running the canary's init path against a real temporary repo.
evidence: B3 states: 'init.py:508-511 sets merge.ours.driver per clone … the canary already gets merge.ours.driver via _merge_ours_unit' — this is a live dependency on a specific code path inside init.py.

B2 states: 'At init.py:366-382 the fetch at :375 runs only if origin/tickets already resolves … control falls through to git worktree add --orphan at :381' — B2 restructures this logic, which is adjacent to the driver setup at :508-511.
B2's 8-item AC list contains no criterion of the form 'rebar init still sets merge.ours.driver=true after B2's changes' or 'the canary's driver setup path is unaffected'.
B3-AC2 is described as a 'unit workflow-lint assertion' — it lints the workflow YAML, not the runtime behavior of `rebar init` after B2 lands.
findings.finding: B2 modifies `init.py` (restructuring the fetch/bootstrap path at :366-382 and the predicate at :628) but includes no acceptance criterion that verifies the `merge.ours.driver` setup code path (`init.py:508-511`, which B3 explicitly relies on) is unaffected by B2's changes. B3's regression guard (B3-AC2) is a workflow-lint unit test written and run at B3's implementation time; it does not continuously re-verify against B2's post-landing state of `init.py`.
scenarios: B2 refactors init.py and inadvertently moves or conditions the _merge_ours_unit call; B3's workflow-lint test still passes (it only checks that the canary YAML calls rebar init, not that rebar init still sets the driver); the canary silently loses its merge driver in production.
B2 and B3 are developed in parallel and land in different PRs; no integration test jointly exercises both changes against the canary worktree.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to B2's acceptance criteria: 'After B2's init.py changes, rebar init still sets merge.ours.driver=true in the worktree git config — verified by the canary's existing rebar-init integration path or an explicit unit assertion on init.py:508-511 surviving the refactor. Tier: unit.' Alternatively, make B3's regression-guard test (AC2) an integration-level test that actually invokes `rebar init` against a temp repo rather than a YAML lint.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the disavowed config-presence check in AC1 with a concrete alternative assertion — e.g., 'a `GIT_TRACE_PACKET` log from the subsequent fetch shows zero pack-objects received, confirming the server honored the filter' — so the executor has an executable positive test.
evidence: 'confirmed to inherit remote.origin.partialclonefilter. Must NOT be a config-presence assertion: git writes that key even when the server ignored the filter (reproduced)'
The plan rejects the observable config key but names no replacement observable — the executor has no executable check to perform.
findings.finding: AC1's 'confirmed to inherit remote.origin.partialclonefilter' sub-criterion explicitly disavows the only natural check (config-presence) but provides no concrete alternative positive test, leaving the executor unable to determine what evidence would satisfy this sub-criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — first bullet (byte measurement AC)
scenarios: An agent implementing B1 passes the CI measurement on pack size but cannot write or evaluate the 'inherit' sub-assertion because the plan has ruled out the only citable artifact without specifying a substitute.
A reviewer reading the closing PR cannot determine whether the inherit criterion is satisfied.
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'Confirm inheritance by running the post-checkout fetch with `GIT_TRACE_PACKET=1` and asserting that the `pack-objects` line reports 0 objects received (i.e., the server applied the filter). Record the raw packet log as a CI artifact.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a concrete numeric pass threshold in AC1 — e.g., 'received pack bytes ≤ 80 MiB (vs ≥ 900 MiB baseline), a ≥ 10× reduction' — rather than relying on 'the expected reduction' with no threshold.
evidence: 'a fresh CI checkout with and without the filter shows the expected reduction'
No numeric threshold or tolerance band appears in the AC itself; 'expected' is implicitly defined by the plan body numbers but not restated in the criterion.
findings.finding: AC1's 'shows the expected reduction' is outcome-vague: the plan body quotes reference measurements (1.04 GiB vs 68.7 MiB, ~15x) but the AC itself states no pass threshold, so an executor cannot determine whether a CI run with, say, a 5x reduction passes or fails.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — first bullet (byte measurement AC)
scenarios: CI pack size drops from 1.04 GiB to 300 MiB (a 3.5x reduction, possibly due to server-side differences) — an agent has no stated threshold to decide pass/fail.
Author and reviewer disagree on whether the measured reduction is sufficient because the bar was never written into the AC.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC1: 'Pass threshold: received pack bytes for the checkout step ≤ 100 MiB (baseline ≥ 900 MiB; target ~15× from the measured 68.7 MiB). Variance up to 2× from the baseline measurement is acceptable given server-side delta compression variability.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the `derive_caused_by` fail-closed contract change (and its rationale: partial path set can elect a wrong culprit) in an ADR or AGENTS.md entry, not only in the clone guidance doc.
evidence: 'make derive_caused_by abort on any per-path blame failure' — this is a behavioral contract change to a shared utility used on the bug-close path.
The AC for this (item 4) validates the None return but does not require documentation of the decision rationale.
The clone-guidance doc AC requires only 'measured numbers' and 'accepted git blame degradation' — it does not require capturing the derive_caused_by contract change.
findings.finding: The decision to change `derive_caused_by` to fail-closed (returning None on ANY per-path blame failure) is a business-rule change with downstream behavioral impact, but it is captured only in a 'clone guidance doc' (B4). This decision changes the contract of `derive_caused_by` for ALL callers — not just in blobless clones — and should be captured in an ADR or AGENTS.md update so future maintainers understand why the function was changed from partial-tally to all-or-nothing.
findings.location: B4 scope item: 'clone guidance doc + make derive_caused_by abort on any per-path blame failure'; AC item 4
scenarios: A future developer calls derive_caused_by expecting a best-effort result and is surprised by None; they 'fix' it back to partial tally, re-introducing the wrong caused_by link bug.
The rationale (wrong culprit from partial path set) is lost when the clone guidance doc is eventually updated or replaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short ADR or AGENTS.md section explaining: (1) prior behavior (partial tally), (2) the failure mode it produced (wrong caused_by link), (3) new contract (None on any per-path failure), (4) accepted consequence (no link rather than wrong link).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either update the plan title to reflect the full scope (e.g., '…+ fix authorship resolver parsing and remove stale backup blob') or move B5 and B6 to a separate plan/child ticket and remove their ACs from this plan.
evidence: Title: 'Cut tickets-store clone cost via CI partial clone + fail closed instead of bootstrapping an empty store'
B5: 'add --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false to the two authorship resolvers'
B6: 'delete .bridge_state.bak-retarget (33,025,572 bytes sitting in the tree at HEAD)'
Neither B5 nor B6 appears in the Context, Approach, or Compatibility sections as a motivated consequence of the clone-cost or fail-closed work.
findings.finding: The plan does MORE than the title promises: B5 (adding --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false to authorship resolvers) and B6 (deleting .bridge_state.bak-retarget) are unrelated to clone-cost reduction or the fail-closed fix, yet are included as first-class scope children with their own ACs. A reader or agent asked to implement the plan from the title alone would not anticipate these tasks, and the title provides no signal that authorship resolver flag hygiene or large-file cleanup are in scope.
scenarios: An agent implementing 'cut clone cost + fail closed' skips B5/B6 because the title gives no hint they are in scope, leading to incomplete delivery.
A reviewer approving the plan as scoped to the title is surprised to find authorship and cleanup changes in the diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to: 'Cut tickets-store clone cost via CI partial clone, fail closed on bootstrap, fix authorship-resolver flag hygiene, and remove stale .bridge_state.bak-retarget' — or split B5/B6 into a companion cleanup ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Split B4 into two separate children: one for the clone-guidance documentation (with measured numbers) and one for the `derive_caused_by` abort-on-failure code fix, so each can land and be reviewed independently.
evidence: 'B4 clone guidance doc + make derive_caused_by abort on any per-path blame failure'
AC item: 'derive_caused_by returns None when blame fails on any path' (pure code correctness)
AC item: 'The clone-guidance doc exists and states the measured numbers' (pure documentation)
These two ACs map to different artifacts with different reviewers/stakeholders and neither depends on the other
findings.finding: Child B4 (vegan-lowish-liger) bundles two independently-releasable outcomes: (1) a clone-guidance documentation artifact (with measured numbers) and (2) a code-correctness fix making `derive_caused_by` abort on any per-path blame failure. These serve different purposes, have different reasons to change (ops/infra documentation vs. blame-attribution correctness), and are each independently valuable and testable — the doc can ship without the code fix and vice versa.
findings.location: Scope section, B4 bullet; child ticket vegan-lowish-liger
scenarios: The code fix for derive_caused_by is urgent (wrong caused_by links written) but the doc is not, or vice versa; bundling them delays whichever is ready first.
A reviewer approving the documentation cannot independently validate the code fix, increasing review cognitive load.
findings.suggested_fix: Create a B4a child for the clone-guidance doc (acceptance: doc exists with measured 1.04 GiB / 68.7 MiB numbers and stated blame-degradation caveat) and a B4b child for the derive_caused_by code fix (acceptance: unit test injecting a per-path failure asserts no link event is written).
